anomaly_def.Name: MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located in the multi-version concurrency-control bookkeeping layer, where obsolete row versions, rollback records, and logically deleted index entries accumulate faster than background cleanup workers can reclaim them. It is distinct from lock contention because the failure mode is version-store growth and visibility-check overhead rather than blocking on lock objects. Observable phenomena: rising ratios of obsolete to live rows reported by table-statistics views, growing version-store or rollback-segment length, increasing physical size of tables and indexes alongside declining live-row density per page, longer sequential scans, planner misestimates caused by the bloated heap, cleanup workers continuously busy or visibly falling behind, and engine warnings about impending transaction-id horizon or version-store wraparound. Possible contributing factors: heavy update and delete churn under page-fill settings that prevent in-place updates, long idle-in-transaction sessions or replication-state objects holding old read snapshots, cleanup worker thresholds and cost limits set too conservatively for the workload, insufficient maintenance memory or I/O budget, large batch deletes without partition rotation, and cleanup workers disabled or under-resourced.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the timeout in seconds for attempts to acquire metadata locks.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_wait_timeout while attempting to acquire a metadata lock.
entry.workload_impact: The metadata lock acquisition fails and the statement does not proceed.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
